verses.text: These were the divisions of the sons of Aaron. The sons of Aaron: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
But Nadab and Abihu died before their father, and had no children: therefore Eleazar and Ithamar executed the priest’s office.
David with Zadok of the sons of Eleazar and Ahimelech of the sons of Ithamar, divided them according to their ordering in their service.

There were more chief men found of the sons of Eleazar than of the sons of Ithamar; and they were divided like this: of the sons of Eleazar there were sixteen, heads of fathers’ houses; and of the sons of Ithamar, according to their fathers’ houses, eight.
Thus were they divided impartially by drawing lots; for there were princes of the sanctuary, and princes of God, both of the sons of Eleazar, and of the sons of Ithamar.

Shemaiah the son of Nethanel the scribe, who was of the Levites, wrote them in the presence of the king, the princes, Zadok the priest, Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, and the heads of the fathers’ households of the priests and of the Levites; one fathers’ house being taken for Eleazar, and one taken for Ithamar.
Now the first lot came out to Jehoiarib, the second to Jedaiah,
the third to Harim, the fourth to Seorim,
the fifth to Malchijah, the sixth to Mijamin,
the seventh to Hakkoz, the eighth to Abijah,
the ninth to Jeshua, the tenth to Shecaniah,
the eleventh to Eliashib, the twelfth to Jakim,
the thirteenth to Huppah, the fourteenth to Jeshebeab,
the fifteenth to Bilgah, the sixteenth to Immer,
the seventeenth to Hezir, the eighteenth to Happizzez,
the nineteenth to Pethahiah, the twentieth to Jehezkel,
the twenty-first to Jachin, the twenty-second to Gamul,
the twenty-third to Delaiah, and the twenty-fourth to Maaziah.
This was their ordering in their service, to come into Yahweh’s house according to the ordinance given to them by Aaron their father, as Yahweh, the God of Israel, had commanded him.
Of the rest of the sons of Levi: of the sons of Amram, Shubael; of the sons of Shubael, Jehdeiah.
Of Rehabiah: of the sons of Rehabiah, Isshiah the chief.
Of the Izharites, Shelomoth; of the sons of Shelomoth, Jahath.
The sons of Hebron: Jeriah, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
The sons of Uzziel: Micah; of the sons of Micah, Shamir.
The brother of Micah: Isshiah; of the sons of Isshiah, Zechariah.
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The son of Jaaziah: Beno.
The sons of Merari: of Jaaziah, Beno, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri.
Of Mahli: Eleazar, who had no sons.
Of Kish, the son of Kish: Jerahmeel.
The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth. These were the sons of the Levites after their fathers’ houses.

These likewise cast lots even as their brothers the sons of Aaron in the presence of David the king, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the fathers’ households of the priests and of the Levites; the fathers’ households of the chief even as those of his younger brother.

footnotes.content: Here we see Aaron's line carefully marked out—Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. These are not names in a ledger alone; they are servants set apart, and we watch how the Lord's hand guides their office through generations. The office itself is the gift.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When Nadab and Abihu died before their father, something hard happened that the community had to reckon with. Yet the office didn't vanish—Eleazar and Ithamar stepped in. Even in loss, God's work continues steadily forward.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David worked with Zadok and Ahimelech to bring order to the priestly divisions. There's a beautiful picture here of leaders—even a king—working alongside priests to serve something greater than themselves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: More chiefs descended from Eleazar than Ithamar, yet all were divided fairly for service. God doesn't shortchange the smaller branch; He gives each what they need to serve. There's a mercy in impartiality.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Drawing lots settles the matter—no favoritism, no quarrel. Both lines of Eleazar and Ithamar are honored equally as princes of the sanctuary. When we trust the lot rather than our own judgment, we often find peace beneath the decision.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shemaiah the scribe wrote these divisions in the presence of the king, the princes, Zadok, and Ahimelech—a record made openly, witnessed by all. This is how authority preserves itself: through clarity, witness, and written memory. The same care we see here echoes in how the Lord keeps His promises written and sure.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The twenty-four lots fell in order: Jehoiarib, Jedaiah, Harim, Seorim, and the rest—each name marks a family entrusted with weeks of service in the house of God. These men knew their place and their time; they belonged to something larger than themselves. To be numbered among God's servants is to rest in that calling.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "This was their ordering in their service, to come into Yahweh's house according to the ordinance given to them by Aaron their father, as Yahweh, the God of Israel, had commanded him." Order flows from God's command through Aaron to these families. When we serve, we serve not by our own will but by commission passed down through the generations of faith.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Of the remaining Levites—not all priests, but all set apart for the house of God's service. Shubael, Jehdeiah, and the others served in different roles, different times, yet all held the same trust. The Body of Christ works the same way, many members, many gifts, one calling.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rehabiah's line continued; Isshiah the chief led them. Notice how the genealogy tracks leadership—not merely inheritance, but the actual passing of responsibility from one generation to the next. Faithfulness leaves traces.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Izharites—Shelomoth and Jahath—represent another branch of the great tree of Levitical service. Each name was known; each family had their role. To be remembered by name in God's house is to matter.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons of Hebron: Jeriah, Amariah, Jahaziel, Jekameam. These four brothers found their calling together, counted in the order of service. When siblings serve the Lord side by side, something beautiful strengthens the whole family.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Micah of the Uzziel line, and his son Shamir—father and son together in the genealogy, father and son together in God's work. This is how faithfulness multiplies across time.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Isshiah, Micah's brother, led his own line—Zechariah their son. Again, brothers dividing the work, both honored. The Lord doesn't measure worth by which son gets which task; He measures it by faithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Mahli and Mushi of the Merari line, Beno son of Jaaziah—the genealogy branches further. Each name is a thread in the great tapestry of worship. When you feel small in God's house, remember: you are part of something ancient and eternal.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons of Merari through Jaaziah: Beno, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri. These four carried their father's name forward in service. To be named and numbered among God's servants is a trust that reaches beyond a lifetime.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Eleazar of the Mahli line had no sons, yet he is still written down, still remembered, still part of the ordained order. A man's worth is not measured by the heirs he leaves behind, but by the faithfulness with which he served.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Of Kish, Jerahmeel—brief lines that carry weight. Not every name gets a story, but every name in God's genealogy matters. The Lord remembers those who serve in obscurity with the same care He remembers the great.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons of Mushi—Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth—complete the roster "after their fathers' houses." Each family branch organized, each generation linked to the last. Order is a gift the Lord gives His people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "These likewise cast lots even as their brothers the sons of Aaron..."—the Levites shared in the same ordering, the same visibility before God and king alike. Readers today hear an echo of that same truth: when we gather to serve the Lord, we are not unseen. We are numbered, remembered, and given our place in His house. As of 2026-10, that promise still holds.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
